summary: Port reproduces the same three-scene crossfading show in the same order and with the same dwell:fade proportion, but its whole clock runs ~20-30% slow (15.00 s cycle vs 17.95 s) and two of the three scenes are quantitatively off: the rainbow-bar scene draws 5 bars instead of 8, and the hue-wave scene uses half the original's hue range with its detail zone parked at the wrong end of the strip.
observations: Both sides compile and render with no runtime errors; neither binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both); neither exposes any control (controls [] on both, probe reports 'no settable controls' for both sides) - control surfaces match.

Structure of the show matches: both cycle through three scenes in the same order - (A) a full-field hue wave, (B) rainbow bars on black, (C) a single red dot bouncing on black - with a crossfade between each.

Cycle length diverges. Autocorrelation of meanBrightness over a 120 s / 5 fps survey gives a first strong peak at exactly 15.0 s on the original (harmonics at 30/45/60 s, all 1.00) and 17.9-18.0 s on the port (harmonics 35.8/53.6 s). Confirmed identical at 5, 10 and 20 fps (orig 75/150/300-frame lags, port 90/179/359), so both sides are time-based, not frame-stepped - the port's cycle is genuinely ~20% too long.

Slot proportions inside the cycle DO match. Original: 3.0 s dwell + 2.0 s crossfade per scene (5.0 s slot x 3 = 15 s); port: ~3.6 s dwell + ~2.4 s crossfade (~6.0 s slot x 3 = 18 s). Same 3:2 dwell:fade ratio, uniformly 1.2x stretched.

Scene B (rainbow bars): the original draws 8 lit bars separated by 8 equal black gaps - run-length dump on the default 16x16 grid read as a rock-steady '-16 +16' x8 (period 32 px of 256) at every sampled time from 5.4 s to 9.2 s. The port draws 5 bars: '-26 +26 -25 +26 -25 +26 -26 +25 -26 +25' (period ~51 px). Bars are static in position on both sides; only the hue scrolls through them.

Both sides are resolution-independent, and the bar-count gap follows the pattern, not the rig: at 32x32 (1024 px) orig is '-64 +64' x8 and port '-103 +102' x5; at 8x8 (64 px) orig is '-4 +4' x8 and port '-7 +6' x5.
Scene B hue geometry matches exactly: on both sides hue advances 6 channel-units per pixel, i.e. one full hue wrap across the whole strip, same direction.
Scene B hue scroll SPEED differs: sampling hue at a fixed pixel index across the dwell gives the original +0.333 hue/s (a full rainbow cycle every 3.00 s) and the port +0.252 hue/s (~3.96 s).

Scene C (red ember): both draw one pure-red dot with a triangular falloff that bounces edge to edge along the strip. Original: 6 lit pixels, peak ~237, travelling 42.7 px per 0.25 s = ~171 px/s (a full there-and-back in ~3.0 s). Port: 8 lit pixels, peak ~224-249, travelling 32.7 px per 0.25 s = ~131 px/s (round trip ~3.9 s). Same behaviour, ~30% slower and a slightly fatter dot.

So both internal animation clocks (scene B hue scroll, scene C bounce) sit at 3.00 s on the original and ~3.9-4.0 s on the port - a ~1.32x stretch, distinct from the 1.2x stretch of the crossfade schedule.

Scene A (hue wave): on both sides it is a fully saturated (sat 1.00), spatially uniform-brightness hue wave along the strip. But the hue excursion differs by 2x - the original sweeps exactly hue 0.500-0.833 (cyan through blue to magenta) at every sampled frame, the port only 0.600-0.760 (blue through violet). Visually the original's scene A reads bright cyan-and-magenta, the port's reads uniformly blue-violet.

Scene A detail placement differs. Measuring per-16-pixel-block spatial roughness across the dwell, the original's high-spatial-frequency zone sits around pixels ~176-215 (75-84% along the strip) and slowly meanders back and forth in time (peak block drifts 12 -> 13 -> 10 over 3 s); the port's sits pinned at pixels 0-30 (the very start of the strip) and does not move at all (roughness profile essentially frozen: 26,12-15,7-12,... on every frame from 0.15 s to 2.95 s). The strip-rig waterfall shows this plainly: the original has a snaking braided band three-quarters of the way across, the port has a static rippled band hard against the left edge.

Scene A global brightness: the original breathes noticeably within its dwell (uniform value 215 -> 250 -> 131 -> 168 over 0.15-2.95 s, a non-monotonic dip in the middle of the dwell, not the crossfade); the port rises and falls in a single shallow arc (214 -> 254 -> 201) with no mid-dwell dip.
Nothing is stochastic: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give byte-identical 60 s survey stats on both sides.
Neither side degrades over time - both brightnessTrend 'volatile' (the cycle), no drift between first and last cycle in the 120 s survey, port zeroMotionFrames 1 of 300.
feedback: Slow everything down by the right factors, but note there are TWO separate clocks and they are wrong by different amounts. The scene schedule (dwell + crossfade) should be 5.0 s per scene / 15.0 s per full cycle, not ~6.0 s / ~18.0 s - shorten it by 1/6. The dwell:fade split is already right at 3:2, keep it.

The internal animation clock is ~32% too slow and should be a 3.00 s period: scene B's rainbow should complete one full hue wrap every 3.00 s (port currently ~3.96 s), and scene C's red dot should cross the strip in 1.5 s / round-trip in 3.0 s, i.e. ~171 px/s on a 256-px rig (port currently ~131 px/s, round trip ~3.9 s).

Scene B (rainbow bars) must draw 8 bars with 8 equal black gaps, i.e. a 50%-duty square wave with 8 cycles across the whole strip. The port draws 5 (period ~51 px instead of 32 px on 256). This is resolution-independent on both sides, so the fix is the cycle count, not a pixel-count normalisation.
Scene B's hue-vs-position gradient is already exactly right (one full hue wrap across the strip, same direction) - do not touch it.

Scene A's hue range is half as wide as it should be. The original sweeps hue 0.500 to 0.833 (cyan -> blue -> magenta, a third of the wheel); the port only reaches 0.600 to 0.760. Widen the wave amplitude so the extremes hit cyan and magenta. Centre is already about right (~0.67).

Scene A's fine-detail zone is in the wrong place and is frozen. On the original the high-spatial-frequency part of the wave lives around 75-85% along the strip and slowly wanders back and forth over a few seconds; on the port it is stuck at the strip's start (first ~30 px of 256) and never moves. Whatever positions the wave's compression should be a slowly time-varying offset near the far end of the strip, not a fixed anchor at index 0.

Scene A should also breathe in overall brightness within its dwell - the original's uniform value goes 250 -> 131 -> 168 mid-dwell (a clear dip and partial recovery before the crossfade begins); the port holds a single shallow arc between 201 and 254.

Scene C is the closest match - same single pure-red dot, same triangular falloff, same edge-to-edge bounce. Only two nitpicks: the dot is 8 lit pixels wide on the port vs 6 on the original, and the speed (above).
